kurzbeschreibung: Imst is the gateway to the Ötztaler Alpen – a city steeped in tradition, vibrant with Fasching celebrations, and brimming with alpine charm.
beschreibung: The district of Imst is located in the Upper Inn Valley and includes the town of Imst as well as the surrounding valley communities. The town of Imst is famous for its Imster Fasching, a traditional carnival festival held every four years, one of Tirol’s oldest with magnificent Schellerlaufen costumes. The region is a paradise for climbers and mountain bikers, featuring the renowned Klettergarten Imst and an extensive mountain bike trail network. In winter, the Hoch-Imst ski area beckons with guaranteed snow reliability. The surrounding area offers access to the wild and romantic valleys of the Gurgltal and the Pitztal.
tipps: The Imst Schemenlaufen carnival takes place only every 4 years – next scheduled for 2027!
The 'Imster Bergl' mountain bike trail is one of the most rewarding and challenging rides in the Oberland.
The Gurgltal mineral trail near Tarrenz is an insider tip for family hikes.
empfehlungen: Explore the historic Altstadt of Imst with its arcaded courtyards and the baroque parish tower. Then try a climbing session at the Klettergarten Imst or hike up to the Muttekopfhütte (2,034 m).
umgebung: The Imst region is located in the Upper Inn Valley, nestled between the Tschirgant in the north and the Ötztaler Alpen in the south. Neighboring regions include: Ötztal (south), Pitztal (west), Telfs (east), and Außerfern (north via the Fernpass). Nearest major city: Innsbruck (50 km away).
